title: item.json — the identity of a library item
description:
Written once, when the item is created, and never touched again: everything here is either true forever or the item is a different item. It is the only file that has to exist in an item folder.

Layout:
  movies/<aa>/<itemId>/item.json
  series/<aa>/<seriesId>/item.json, episodes/<episodeId>/item.json

<aa> is the first two characters of the id. There is no title change here, no revision and no updatedAt: a renamed title is a database change that reaches storage through metadata.json, and everything that happens to the item after creation is a version, a package or an event.

itemId.description: Equals the name of the folder this file sits in, and its first two characters are the shard folder.

title.description: The title as it was at creation, for human orientation in a folder listing. It is not the display title: that is projected into metadata.json and may differ.

externalIds.description: The reference ids the item was created with. Enough to fetch its texts and images again.

createdAt.description: When the item entered the library. It orders 'recently added', so it must survive every migration unchanged.

createdBy.description: The service or person that created the item.

provenance.description: How the item came to exist, when it came from somewhere else. It is part of the item's creation, so it is written once with the rest of this file and never revised. A tree built by migrating an old catalog keeps the old ids here, so what was already known about the item can still be found after the catalog it came from is gone.

legacyItemId.description: The id the item had in the catalog it came from.

seriesId.description: Episode only: the series folder two levels up.

episodeCode.description: Episode only, e.g. 'S01E03'. Agrees with seasonNumber and episodeNumber.
